hemomancy.acolyte.about_clarity.line1: Clarity comes after purity. You quiet the infection first, and then you learn to see without the fever getting in the way.
hemomancy.acolyte.about_clarity.line2: Consecrated copper teaches endurance, I think, or that's how it was explained to me: it changed and oxidized, and then it settled and stayed that way.
hemomancy.acolyte.about_clarity.line3: Once your blood's fully pale, that lesson can stop being a wound and become a halo.
hemomancy.acolyte.absolved.line1: Most of the old red's gone pale now. It's all right to mourn it. A lot of people do.
hemomancy.acolyte.absolved.line2: Let the grief run through clean water and out of you. Whatever's left after that is yours, in a way the blood never was.
hemomancy.acolyte.clarity.line1: The second water's taken you. With your blood this quiet, the rest of the world gets loud. Does it feel like too much, some days?
hemomancy.acolyte.clarity.line2: Sharp sight can still lie to you, and a clear eye can turn merciless without ever noticing it has.
hemomancy.acolyte.cleansing.line1: You're in the long middle now, where the blood's learned to be afraid and frightened things hold on harder.
hemomancy.acolyte.cleansing.line2: The Rite of the Silver Veil lays a ward over you for a while, and if you walk it, I'd take the ward as an instruction to leave the closing wound alone.
hemomancy.acolyte.corrupted.line1: The first dose opened the wound, and I know it hurts, but it hurts because the blood-memory isn't so sure of itself anymore.
hemomancy.acolyte.corrupted.line2: Be careful with it, though. The old current still answers if you call, and each time you do, it learns your name again.
hemomancy.acolyte.enlightened.line1: §7[The Acolyte bows until their forehead nearly touches their clasped hands]
hemomancy.acolyte.enlightened.line2: I can't always tell if the Lady weeps for joy or as a warning. Among the Unstained it tends to be the same water.
hemomancy.acolyte.how_clarity.line1: Consecrated copper at the podium readies you, and the Rite of Clarity Ascension is what wakes it. After that it deepens through offerings that teach you to perceive things instead of hungering for them, or so I've been taught.
hemomancy.acolyte.how_clarity.line2: Silver chalices help. So does hemolytic plating, and the verdigris rites, if you can stand them. All of it strengthens the halo your purity made room for.
hemomancy.acolyte.how_purify.line1: Purity grows when you hold back and show mercy, I think, and through offerings that don't ask anything of blood.
hemomancy.acolyte.how_purify.line2: Hemolytic solution at the podium readies you, and the Lethean Baptism begins it. After that it's Lethean flowers and pale dew, sleep, clean labor, and the animals you raise and tend.
hemomancy.acolyte.how_purify.line3: Don't rush it, please, because if you close a wound too fast, the rot stays under the skin.
hemomancy.acolyte.lady_lore.line1: Our Lady of Still Waters lives wherever a fever breaks, or that's how I was taught to say it. She belongs to this world, down in the cold water, not up in some heaven.
hemomancy.acolyte.lady_lore.line2: When the crimson fungus spread through blood and memory, the world fought it the way a body fights an infection. That part I believe without trying.
hemomancy.acolyte.lady_lore.line3: She's that answer with a face on it, and patience, and she's defensive rather than cruel. There's someone in the stillness, though I couldn't tell you who.
hemomancy.acolyte.not_on_path.line1: §7[The Acolyte lowers their voice as the church air cools around you]
hemomancy.acolyte.not_on_path.line2: You haven't started the washing yet. If the blood's troubling you, a Zealot can talk it through with you, and then you'd bring hemolytic solution to the podium.
hemomancy.acolyte.purified.line1: Your blood's white now, the way bone goes white in winter, and the first transformation has set for good.
hemomancy.acolyte.purified.line2: If you want clarity, bring consecrated copper to the podium, then walk the Rite of Clarity Ascension and let the last crimson habit go quiet. There's no hurry, at least none that I've seen.
hemomancy.acolyte.silver_veil.line1: I think of the Silver Veil as purification's inner skin. It holds the crimson current away from you.
hemomancy.acolyte.silver_veil.line2: Once there's some distance between you and it, you can make your own choice.
hemomancy.acolyte.tainted.line1: The stain's thinning, and you might feel hollow in the places where power used to answer you. I hope you're sleeping all right.
hemomancy.acolyte.tainted.line2: I've come to think of that hollow as room you're getting back.
hemomancy.acolyte.verdigris.line1: Verdigris is what copper turns into after a long exposure. It's changed, but it still does its job, and I like that about it.
hemomancy.acolyte.verdigris.line2: Nobody comes to purity untouched, not even the ones who've been here longest. You get there by surviving the contact honestly.
hemomancy.acolyte.who_are_you.line1: We keep the still water. Mostly that means we sit with people and witness what the infection does to them, and only after that does anyone here judge, though it does come to that sometimes.
hemomancy.acolyte.who_are_you.line2: Some of us were Harbingers, and some had Harbingers in the family. A few of us mostly came for the people. Every one of us knows it's easier to inherit the crimson than to get rid of it.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.chisel_lore: "Chisel Station" is the old recipe's name for the Cerebral Scarring Station, and there's only the one bench. You cut the pattern into a blank scar with a knapper in the tool slot, and every carving wears the knapper down, more for a longer pattern. Learn the pattern before you cut, because I'd rather you found your mistakes on paper.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.crimson_vessel: At Degree 4, the white gourd can become the Crimson Vessel. Offer your Pallid Vessel and an amethyst shard at a Greater Working floor, fill its four anchors, wake the Bastion support sigil it needs, and project into the daemon. You won't get the Pallid Vessel back. The red one holds 1,800 mL and feeds blood back faster than the white gourd did.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.lantern.line1: You've been able to build a Mycelial Lantern since the third Degree. Have you? Keep a culture alive in one and you can stop spending every enzyme the moment you find it.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.lantern.line2: Set spores in the culture slot and feed it blood. It'll keep fruiting the matching enzyme for as long as the culture stays in place. Empty the output before it fills up.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.line1: §7[The Alchemist sets a pair of forceps down on the bench and wipes their hands before turning round]
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.line2: Word is you're an Adept. I've watched you run the machines, so now for the stations that work on you. The sample's you, this time.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.morphlings.lin: A wild Morphling polyp is a living specimen. It doesn't carry any of your instructions, so don't handle it like a puppet.
Bring me a supported polyp in a specimen jar and we'll record what it might become. The Incubator comes later, and you don't need it, or a forced fight, to start observing them.
hemomancy.alchemist.adept.scar_station_l: Treat the Cerebral Scarring Station as a surgical instrument that happens to look like a crafting bench. You carve a pattern into a blank scar with a knapper, and that's all the bench does. Learning the carved scar happens at an Iron Brazier, and the Vein-Mason teaches that part. Once you've learned it, its route opens new neural and venous pathways, and that changes the manipulations you can sustain and how strongly your tendencies show.
hemomancy.alchemist.apotheos.line1: §4[The Alchemist sets down the flask they were holding, very carefully, and keeps a hand on it for a moment after]
hemomancy.alchemist.apotheos.line2: So that's Apotheos. I tried to take a reading off you when you came in, and I can't make sense of it. The machines still run, though, so if you left anything unfinished, I'll help with it.
hemomancy.alchemist.apotheos.reflection: §oI used to think the Alembic, the Centrifuge, the Loom and the Incubator were as far as the work went. I kept a list of improvements for each of them. §4§oYou§r weren't on the list, and I still don't know which column to put you in.
hemomancy.alchemist.archon.line1: §4[The Alchemist straightens up from the bench, then, after a moment, bows their head]
hemomancy.alchemist.archon.line2: Archon. The workshop's still open to you. Anything that needs preparing or repairing?
hemomancy.alchemist.armor_research.barbe: Catalog a Barbed Urchin, a Desiccant, and a Venom Rib Centipede.
Records only. Their spines and venom tell me more about the Barbed answer than another surrendered carcass would.
hemomancy.alchemist.armor_research.chiti: Catalog a Chalybeate Snail, a Chitinite, and a Fervent Chitinite.
Records again, no bodies. Their shells show the Artificer where Chitinite armor can give without breaking.
hemomancy.alchemist.armor_research.claim: Your Bestiary has the three records I asked for. I'll check them against the Artificer's work before I issue another reagent.
hemomancy.alchemist.armor_research.prism: Catalog a Prism Cuttle, a Scarlet Serpent, and a Verdigris Moth.
No bodies this time either. I want to see how their pigments shift, because that's what the Prismatic answer is copying.
hemomancy.alchemist.artificer_crimson_ve: Your consecrated frame's been inspected, so I'll issue the Crimson Lacquer you need to finish the vestment.
hemomancy.alchemist.artificer_three_answ: The Artificer's inspection is good enough for me. I've got the reagent that matches the armor family you chose, so take it and put that answer to work.
hemomancy.alchemist.bloodwood_lesson.lin: Bloodwood starts from any sapling. Project your active blood into it until it's taken 900 mL, and you don't have to do it in one cast.
Where are you planting it? Open ground, with room: the limbs need replaceable space up to eight blocks out and thirteen above the sapling. The leaves will grow around whatever's in their way.

A Dead Bush is the worse idea. 1,800 mL and it comes up as Heartwood, no leaves, still hungry. It bleeds whatever touches it and anyone within four blocks, and all of that drains into one core in the trunk. Fill the core until it burns deep red, 1,800 mL by projection or about nine cows, and only then cut it out for Ravenous Heartwood. Cut early and you've got a log.
hemomancy.alchemist.body_answers.line1: You've separated blood by tendency. Now stop thinking of those answers as ingredients and nothing else.
hemomancy.alchemist.body_answers.line2: Sanguine Formation goes in the Alembic and Fervent Enzyme in the catalyst slot. Empty the Bloody Flask I gave you into the tank through the lower-right container input. The clay flask comes back in the output, so put that same flask into the same input. A brew takes 2,500 mL from the tank and fills the empty flask with the tincture. Tank running low? Top it up with Projection.
hemomancy.alchemist.body_answers.line3: Then drink it. Your arms learn the Thelemic Memory Sanguine Fists and hold a reserve of the preparation. Pick it from the same radial as what the Mnemonist calls your Noetic Memories, and activate it. You'll keep what you've learned. Every use still costs blood and strains the vessels it runs through.
hemomancy.alchemist.body_answers.prompt: You know what blood separates into now. Next I can show you how those answers get brewed back into the body.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.athanor.clai: Once it's seated, the Athanor's new socket takes your second catalyst, and the tank keeps the Condenser's 7,500 mL capacity. The mantle keeps itself hot, so it needs no block underneath, and every Alembic recipe runs in half the time. Cancel the rite and you get every offering back, though not the blood you've already put in. A finished Athanor keeps its tier when you move it.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.athanor.prom: Your Condenser work checks out. I can release the Athanor Kit and show you the greater circuit.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.athanor.read: This Athanor Kit goes to a Condenser on a working greater Cardinal floor. Put it on a lit brazier with five more offerings, then feed the three marked bulbs in order.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.athanor.requ: I want to see your own hands on it. Take a distillation result out yourself, then finish a refinement and a two-effect compound at a Condenser and take each of those out too. Reach the sixth Degree with your blood awake and the greater circuit's yours, whether or not you ever took my earlier kit.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.condenser.cl: The Condenser Kit's yours, and you know how to build another if this one goes wrong. Cancel the rite and every offering comes back. A finished Condenser takes your tank from 5,000 to 7,500 mL. It won't fill the extra for you, and it keeps that capacity if you move it.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.condenser.pr: You've done the lesser work and brought me enough evidence. I can release the Condenser Kit and walk you through the rite that seats it.
hemomancy.alchemist.brewing.condenser.re: You've seen what the Alembic separates. Take this Condenser Kit to a lit brazier on a working lesser Cardinal floor and put five more offerings beside it. The Alembic sits one plinth behind the Focus, and its two blood circuits have to close in order.
Distill something at an ordinary Alembic and take the result out yourself. Once you've reached the fourth Degree with your blood awake, I'll trust you with a Condenser kit.
hemomancy.alchemist.centrifuge.fractiona: With the fractionating rotor a spin takes five seconds and gives you half again as much primary material, on average. Every ordinary vial leaves one iron powder. Half of your mixed specimens will also give up one item of a different fraction, and it only ever comes from that specimen's own blood profile. Both fractions share the eight output slots, so keep them clear. Sacred syringes still yield one residuum.
You've worked the calibrated rotor. I can teach you to recover a second fraction.

A mixed specimen can still have another useful fraction left in it. Set this kit on a lit brazier with an Amethyst Shard, a Ghast Tear, a Hematic Iron Block, Chromatic Sublimate and an Enzyme Primer. The calibrated centrifuge goes two blocks behind the Focus on a Greater working floor. Fill eight anchors, close three 50 mL circuits, then finish the procession.

Take an ordinary specimen result out of a completed calibrated or fractionating spin yourself. Get to the sixth Degree with your blood awake and your earlier separation work proven, and the next rotor's yours. Skipped my first gift? I'm only checking the work.
With the governor fitted, a spin takes seven and a half seconds and gives a quarter more primary material on average, and on average three vials in four leave iron powder behind. You still balance opposing vials. You know how to craft another kit now. Cancel the rite and you get the offerings and the Staff back, but the blood you've spent stays spent.
Your separation work holds up. I can give you a governor and teach you its two circuits.

A steadier spin leaves less behind. Bring this governor to a lit brazier with an Iron Ingot, a Chain, Sanguine Glass, a Ferric Binder and a Neurotic Enzyme. The base centrifuge sits two blocks behind the Focus on a Greater working floor. Fill four anchors, close two 50 mL circuits, then finish the procession.

Balance a spin and take an ordinary specimen result out yourself, which you've already covered in First Separation. Reach the fourth Degree with your blood awake and I can give you a Centrifugal Governor Kit.
hemomancy.alchemist.clarity.line1: §7[The Alchemist looks straight through you, then goes back to their work without a word]
hemomancy.alchemist.court.known.alchemis: I've told you already: the best cultivators aren't ours. Ask a Voyager for the Relay Chart.
hemomancy.alchemist.court.known.found: You found the Court yourself? Then you've seen their beds. Did the strains look healthier there than in my jars?
hemomancy.alchemist.court.known.letter: You've already read their letter, I gather. Good. It saves me a speech I'd have given badly.
hemomancy.alchemist.court.known.voyager: The Voyagers got to you first, then. Fine. They've seen the Court's beds, and I've only ever seen samples.
hemomancy.alchemist.court.lead.line1: That strain's past Mature, so I'll be plain: the best cultivators of these lines aren't in the Order. Our Latin's an outsider's catalog.
hemomancy.alchemist.court.lead.line2: They're at sea. Ask a Voyager, or follow the coast, and if you find them, I'd want a sample of whatever they feed theirs.
hemomancy.alchemist.court.letter_lost: You lost a sealed letter off a drowned Votary? What was the seal? If it was Sunburst crust, it's the Brined Court's, and a Voyager can chart it.
hemomancy.alchemist.deep_dark_commission: There's Deep Dark terrain in the Overworld near X %s, Y %s, Z %s. Find a safe way down and look for a sculk catalyst. You don't need to fight a Warden. That bearing marks a region, so don't count on a safe entrance or a Vigil archive there.
I can't find Deep Dark terrain within 2,048 blocks of here. That doesn't mean there's none farther out, so try asking from another Overworld outpost.
Ask me for a Deep Dark bearing while you're in the Overworld. From here I can't line your position up with anything underground there.

I've got a Deep Dark commission for you. You don't need my permission to go down there, but ask me for a bearing before you leave. A sculk catalyst or a Warden can yield Ahaematic colloid, and whichever you sample goes under a Hematic Microscope, because it isn't ordinary blood.
You've already examined an Ahaematic sample, or carried that analysis into the later replay. I'm not sending you back down for a second one just to open a commission.
The Alchemist records your Ahaematic findings. You keep the sample, and the Vigil inquiry is still yours to finish.
Report the Ahaematic analysis to the Alchemist. You keep the sample.
So what did the sample show? The Vigil Beneath and its recordings are a separate inquiry, and this report won't close them.
hemomancy.alchemist.enzyme_uses.brewing: An ordinary brewing stand will take them too, if you're in a hurry. Vivacious makes Regeneration, Fervent makes Fire Resistance, Neurotic gives Swiftness and Incandescent gives Night Vision. Ruinous gives Poison, Frigid gives Slowness and Ferric gives Strength. Umbral turns Night Vision into Invisibility.
hemomancy.alchemist.enzyme_uses.culture: From Degree 3 you can combine an enzyme with a Spore Sac and Hyphal Substrate to get its matching culture. Put that culture in a Mycelial Lantern and it'll keep fruiting the same enzyme, at 600 blood over 2,400 ticks.
hemomancy.alchemist.enzyme_uses.workshop: Put together, that's your first living workshop: the Centrifuge finds an expression and the culture preserves it. A Gourdvine Tap can supply the Lantern, though you'll still have to gather blood yourself.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_draws.offer: Before you touch the Centrifuge, I want to see you take a clean sample. Here are five empty Blood Vials. If you can't carry them all, I'll hold the rest until you've made room. Left-click ordinary animals with them until you've got five samples from at least three species: cattle, pigs, sheep, chickens, rabbits or goats. Keep the filled vials, you'll want them later. Run short? A glass bottle and redstone dust make another Blood Vial.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_draws.progress: How many species so far? Keep drawing from common animals, because five samples across three species gives you a set worth putting in the Centrifuge. Your next Degree's still the Vicar's call, through the bloodcraft proof.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_separation.bri: Two loose Blood Vials, and if they don't fit, I'll hold them until you've made room. Left-click a cow with each one. The vial cancels the hit, so the cow's fine. Set both samples in opposing Centrifuge slots and recover the Vivacious Enzyme. Then come back for a Living Syringe and a vial rack, and after that I'll teach you the Ghastly Alembic.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_separation.cla: The enzyme came through a balanced spin, then? Show me the result and I'll close the assignment and issue your next supplies.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_separation.com: The enzyme held its shape. Good. Here's your Living Syringe and vial rack, and whatever doesn't fit waits until you've got space. Next, run one ordinary Ghastly Alembic distillation to the end and take the result out. Come back once you have and I'll prepare your Concentrated Blood.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_separation.nex: If you can't carry your tools yet, I'll keep them under the bench. Next I need one completed Ghastly Alembic distillation from you. Take its result out, then ask me for Concentrated Blood.
hemomancy.alchemist.first_separation.off: The Vicar's already tested your hand with blood. Now I'd like to see what you can separate from a living sample.

I call it the First Separation. Draw two samples from cattle, balance the vials opposite each other in a Vial Centrifuge, and recover whatever Vivacious Enzyme survives the spin. Say yes and I'll hand you the empty vials.
hemomancy.alchemist.fungal_survey.ready: Habitat seen, both specimens on you? Then I can record the comparison now.
hemomancy.alchemist.fungal_survey.record: The Alchemist records the Overworld survey and hands both plants back.
hemomancy.alchemist.fungal_survey.report: Show both specimens for inspection. You keep them.
hemomancy.alchemist.fungal_survey.specim: I've recorded your visit. When you report, carry an Infected Fungus and a Puffball Fungus. I'll look them over and hand them back untouched.
hemomancy.alchemist.fungal_survey.visit: Go observe the Fungal Gardens biome in the Overworld first. The projection garden's somewhere else entirely, and it won't tell me anything about the local growth.
hemomancy.alchemist.gourd_use.fill: Put a corked gourd in the Ghastly Alembic's blood-output slot, let it fill from the reservoir, then take it back out. The gourd keeps its own separate reserve. It won't make your body hold any more blood than it did. Fit it in the Scarlet Vanity's gourd slot, or carry it in your pack.
hemomancy.alchemist.gourd_use.withdraw: Use the gourd in your hand to open or cork it. Once it's equipped, use Toggle Gourd Open/Closed, normally H. While it's open, it feeds stored blood back whenever your own reserve's low and your blood is active. Cork it to stop. Empty the old vessel before you offer it for an upgrade. Red comes at Degree 4, Black at Degree 5, the Curved Horn at Degree 6.
hemomancy.alchemist.illuminatus.ashen_ve: At Degree 5, the red gourd goes black. Offer the Crimson Vessel and a ghast tear at a Greater Working floor. Same procedure as last time: fill its four anchors, wake the Bastion support sigil it needs, then project into the daemon. The offering uses up the Crimson Vessel. The black gourd holds 3,500 mL, but it feeds blood back slower than the red one did.
hemomancy.alchemist.illuminatus.incubato: The Morphling Incubator raises cultivated fungal symbionts under controlled conditions. A wild polyp could go several ways, and incubation makes one strain stable enough to live with you.
hemomancy.alchemist.illuminatus.line1: Illuminatus, then. The Crimson Lodge has you now. The machines you'll be working with from here run on principles the uninitiated would call impossible. I'd call them badly documented.
hemomancy.alchemist.initiate.line1: An Initiate. Then you're ready for the Somatic Loom, and most of this Outpost's advanced processes run through it, so you'll be seeing a lot of it.
hemomancy.alchemist.initiate.loom_lore: The Somatic Loom is a physical rite with a machine attached. Prepare a blank vessel and the catalyst, store the enzyme colors it calls for and project blood, and an engram unfurls on the ground around it. Use the Living Staff to thread each of the memory's fragments home along its star, and watch for the false ones. What the memory means is the Mnemonist's department. You build one by raising its frame beside a Cardinal Focus on a Lesser Working floor, and I'll walk you through that separately.
hemomancy.alchemist.initiate.loom_raisin: You build machines on a Lesser Working floor, the same kind the vessel uses. Put the Somatic Loom's frame up beside the Focus and seat a Sanguine Formation. Light its braziers and feed the frame. The floor swallows the frame and forges the Loom.
hemomancy.alchemist.initiate.memory_weav: The Mnemonist will give you the long version, grammar and all. Here's the bench version: the Loom writes the manipulation into the memory, so it's finished before it ever reaches the Reliquary. The Reliquary just switches on what you already know.
hemomancy.alchemist.initiate.mnemonist_b: You've cataloged enough red expression to move on, so take a blank vessel to the Mnemonist. They'll show you how a memory gets made ready before the Loom writes anything into it.
hemomancy.alchemist.initiate.pallid_vess: Offer one Dried Gourd in a lit brazier at a Lesser Working floor. That's bone blocks and polished Venous Stone Bricks around the Focus. Leave the Focus empty and plant your Living Staff. Fill the four anchors with Blood Projection, then project into the daemon. You won't need a helper, a support sigil or an ordeal for this one.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_hint: What are you carrying? Show me and I'll tell you which of it belongs on my bench.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.barbed_: The barbs on a Barbed Blade have living extensions that draw blood on contact, and every hit puts a little back into the wielder's reserve. Over a long fight it adds up.
Carry it when you need to fight and refill your reserve at the same time. When the target has to die quickly, bring something heavier.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.blaze_p: Blaze powder, out of the Nether, and it goes up if you look at it wrong. The Alembic reads that as a good Flammeus tendency input and strips it down into Fervent Enzyme concentrate.
Careful how you carry it. Friction alone can set it off. Keep it dry, keep it away from blood vials, and don't let it near open flame until you mean to use it.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.blood_c: A chip off a blood crystal. It's less pure than a full formation, but it still works as a lower-tier Alembic input, or to round out a recipe.
Hang on to them. The Alembic takes them at a reduced yield, so wait until you've got a batch worth running. A handful isn't worth the run.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.blood_g: The blood gourd's your main storage vessel, and you'll upgrade it as your initiation goes deeper. More room in it means a deeper reserve, and that means longer casting.
White, Red, then Black, and each tier holds more. White's only where you start, so don't get attached.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.bloody_: A Bloody Flask carries blood from one place to another. It has nothing to do with the syringe-and-rack assay, so don't file it there.
Use it when blood has to travel. Machines take either vessel as red fluid, so use whichever's to hand.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.brewing: A brewing stand is what common practitioners distill with. Its water-and-base process gives blunt biological responses. It's the Alembic's rough ancestor, the way boiling meat over a fire comes before learning to cook.
A stand gets you threshold effects, and the Alembic gets you precise tendency concentrates. Knowing your way around a stand won't teach you what the Alembic's doing.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.brine_s: Sunburst crust on the seal. That's a strain's exudate, dried. Whoever sealed this cultivated it.
It's meant for the Brined Court, and a Voyager can chart the way. I'd like a scraping of that seal first.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.cabinet: Nine pigeonholes, sixty-four full vials in each. One exemplar sits on display and the rest stay safely behind it. Loose vials still travel one at a time.

Each pigeonhole takes exact matches only, name and identification included, so examined and unknown samples don't share a hole. Shift-click to deposit or withdraw as many individual vials as will fit.

Want to see the collection with the door shut? Fit a clear glass pane. Sneak-use a Knapper to take it out again, and it won't blunt the Knapper. In survival you get the pane back. In creative the pane costs nothing going in and gives nothing back coming out.

Empty the cabinet before you take it apart. Nothing pushes it, and an ordinary explosion leaves a filled one standing. Break it on purpose in creative and the contents are discarded. A carried cabinet never holds specimens.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.chalybe: Iron sulfide in a living skirt. A ridiculous phrase, and yet the snail makes it work.
Knap it while the creature is withdrawn. If you have to kill it for scraps, you've already botched the material.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.cleansi: Cleansing hemolymph, the blue lytic stuff you get out of Hemolymphopoda and Ice Fish. Its circulatory chemistry eats standard blood-matrix compounds, so keep it well away from my racks.
As a lytic agent it's efficient and stable. What other people use it for isn't my concern.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.dendrit: The Dendritic Distributor saves the arrangement of a whole manipulation loadout as a remembered neural pattern. You learn the memories somewhere else, and this station just keeps them in order.
Saving a pattern or writing over one costs blood and raw experience. The nervous lattice holds three patterns to start with, and you'll open more with deeper synaptic discipline.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.enzyme_: That's Ferric Enzyme, the iron one. Put it in blood and the blood starts behaving like a girder: it carries current and holds its shape. Ferric manipulations use that to harden the body and put energy exactly where it's sent.
You'll concentrate it out of metallic or mineral-heavy organic matter. I've measured its conductivity and it doesn't drift, so it's the one to use when a recipe wants a stable metallic reagent.
Leave a vial of Fervent Enzyme on a warm shelf and the cork works itself loose. That's the Flammeus in it. Its manipulations take the heat in the blood and throw it outward.
Distill combustible compounds in the Alembic, then put the enriched output through the centrifuge.
Frigid Enzyme, from Congeatio. It turns blood cold and slow, and you'll see it crystallizing at the edges of the glass. Its manipulations pin things where they are and keep them from spoiling.
Run materials that naturally preserve or resist cold through the Alembic and you'll get Congeatio.
Incandescent Enzyme is the Lux one. A good sample glows bright enough to read by, and I have. That light is what its manipulations use to fool the eye and bend what can be seen.
Lux concentrates out of luminescent organic materials, so that's what you'll run through the Alembic.
Neurotic Enzyme comes out of Ductilis, and it's nerve and motion in a form I can bottle. Tap the rack and the sample flinches before the glass does.
Reach for it when a recipe needs blood to carry a signal. If the recipe wants a shape held, that's Ferric work.

Ruinous Enzyme, from Mortem. Leave it in a vial long enough and it eats the stopper, and anything else it touches goes the same way. Ruinous manipulations speed up decay and sap the vitality out of a target.
Mortem concentrates in the Alembic out of anything that's decomposing. The Covenant is wary of it, and so am I.
Umbral Enzyme, from Tenebris. Hold a vial of it up to the lamp and the lamp looks dimmer. Umbral manipulations do the same to a person: harder to see, and slower to notice you.
Run anything with a natural affinity for darkness through the Alembic and you'll get Tenebris out of it.

Most people separate Vivacious Enzyme first. It's Animus, whatever keeps a body going when it ought to stop, and its manipulations speed healing, make you faster on your feet and keep the body working under strain.
Distill organic life-force materials in the Alembic first, then run the enriched blood samples through the Vial Centrifuge. It comes out at the end of the spin.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.erythro: Cut it cleanly and it stays useful. Tear it apart and you mostly get wet pulp with ambitions.
The reef grows in beds, so work it like a garden. Take a little from each bed and leave the rest to grow back.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.foul_pa: Foul Paste, a dense organic binder. Keep it sealed, and don't use more than the recipe measures out.
The Alembic makes it from particular organic inputs. Keep a steady supply going, because every interruption wastes reagent.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.fungal_: The Fungal Implantation Pylon puts one cultivated fungal scar into you, and later it can replace that scar or take it out. It won't make room you haven't got, so count your fungal slots first.
At Degree 4, raise its frame beside a Cardinal Focus on a Lesser Working floor, seat Hyphal Substrate in the Focus and feed the frame until the floor takes it.
The implantation pylon is Degree 4 scar work. Cultivate the fungal scar first, and don't build the station until you can use it.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.glass_b: A glass bottle's a common alchemical vessel. It holds liquid and seals well enough, right up until pressure shatters it, and it can't match a blood vial's calibrated volume.
Use it for unstabilized material that's got no business in a blood vial. Anything you mean to distill or separate goes in the proper vessel.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.glowsto: Glowstone dust, from the Nether. The Alembic reads its light as a good Lux tendency input and strips it down into Incandescent Enzyme concentrate.
The Incandescent Enzyme yield's good, and the run comes out clean, with very little to scrape off afterward. For Lux work it's about the most reliable ordinary input there is.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.hematic: Hematic iron scrap is what you get smelting iron that's sat in blood a long time. The metal soaks up trace blood compounds and comes out fire resistant and tougher, and it conducts blood energy a little.
Smelt the scrap into ingots before you use it. Scrap is chemically unstable, and it's the ingot that holds those useful properties steady.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.hemolyt: Hemolytic solution is a lytic compound that breaks blood matrices down at the cellular level. Blood-afflicted organisms depend on that matrix for their structure, and that's why it works on them.
It's made by a different process from standard blood distillation, and it works. That's all I've got to say about it.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.iron_in: Ordinary iron doesn't take blood at all. You learn Hematic Iron through Blood Projection and recover it through the Order's salvage practices. Standing an ingot next to a dramatic furnace does nothing for it.
Use the blood-structure plan, or salvage damaged iron the proven way. A hotter furnace won't help.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.living_: This is biological instruction prepared for a Living Staff. I can tell you whether it's materially stable, but the rite belongs to the Redwright.
Ask the Artificer how the Iron Brazier and Blood Absorption get the staff to accept the limb-pattern. It's his rite.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.minecra: Common apparatus, and still worth reading properly. Its shape, heat tolerance and residue tell me what work it'll survive.
Bring it to a bench when a formula calls for it. Otherwise it's an ordinary thing, however well you know it.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.mnemoni: The Mnemonic Reliquary sorts the bodily and willed memories you already know into your active set. I'd call it a loadout, and the Mnemonist wouldn't.
It doesn't add anything of its own. The memory items do the work, and it just decides which of the ones you know are switched on.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.morphli: Dead Man's Rope throws strands. They catch your falls, and from Mature you can tie one to an ally or a block.
Either end can let go. Have you tried reeling yourself toward a block anchor? It's a decent grapple for a fungus.
Holdfast grips stone. Stand on it, or get underwater, and you're hard to shift.
It won't plate you. It holds you in place and shelters whoever's behind you, and if you sneak into a hit you'll see how it braces.
Hushbell conserves. You get hungry more slowly, you lose air more slowly, and poison doesn't take.
Stand still and it hardens. Take a bad hit and it folds shut around you for a few seconds, and you can't act while it's shut, so plan for that.
The Morphling Incubator stabilizes cultivated fungal symbionts. They're still living dependents, and they keep their own nature.
What develops depends on the strain, the enzyme and your husbandry. The Incubator only sets the conditions, and whatever grows in there won't ask your permission first.
The Morphling Incubator is past your current initiation. Come back when you've reached the fifth Degree.
Ink Cap hides you. Hostiles notice you later, and in the dark or underwater they notice you a good deal later.
At Apex it'll spend 500 mL to keep you alive once and cover your exit in ink. It's for getting away, so don't try to ambush anything with it.
Kinbud stings, and it regrows part of every wound you take over the next ten seconds.
Keep it near heat and it works harder. The second head is still part of your body, so don't expect it to take orders.
Marrowplume feeds on bone and on what a fight leaves. Near bone blocks, or right after a kill, it heals you faster.
From Apex, kills may yield more, and always a bone. Players, bosses and spawner stock are excluded, before you ask.
Mermaid's Purse banks blood from your strikes and spends it on whoever's bleeding worst. That includes you.
It feeds best at speed: sprint-swim before you strike and the yield goes up by half. Bring company, too, because it likes a school.
Sunburst feeds on sunlight through an alga it keeps in its tissue. Wear it under open sky and it covers its own upkeep.
Under a roof it costs blood like any other strain. Watch it when someone near you is failing, because it feeds them before it looks after you.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.nether_: Nether Wart is the usual base catalyst in common brewing. In the Alembic its organic structure binds volatile distillations that would otherwise throw off waste compounds.
So in the Alembic it steadies the process. If a run keeps giving you erratic or unstable output, add some.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.recycle: Recycled Enzyme is salvage-grade reagent, and it's weaker and less specific than a fresh separation.
Dismantle a learned memory and you won't get any enzyme back, because the modern Loom keeps what it weaves.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.redston: Redstone. Engineers use it to carry a signal, and there's enough blood-mineral in it that the Alembic reads it as Ferric tendency input.
It makes sense once you've worked with both. Ferric blood carries current and holds structure, and redstone does much the same job in a mechanism, so the Alembic treats them alike.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.refusal: I know what that is. I'm not teaching blood-work to someone who's busy washing their blood out.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.salt_st: Field logs are full of errors, and some of them are worth having. Someone tested reef tissue, vent scale and seawater in the same alembic and lived long enough to write annoyed corrections.
Treat any sample from that wreck as contaminated by both salt and devotion.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.sanguin: Sanguine Formation, crystallized blood mineral. Project blood into an empty cauldron and leave it, and in time you'll find this condensed at the bottom.
In a bare cauldron the shape sometimes slumps back to nothing. Raise the cauldron through the Vicar's Working rites and it'll hold more, set faster and lose none.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.scar_bl: A blank scar. It's stock for the Cerebral Scarring Station, and the pattern and catalyst you use decide which route gets carved into it.

Once it's carved, set it in an empty Iron Brazier and light it with Blood Projection. Hold Blood Absorption on the offering and you learn the route, for 100 mL. It goes in the Brazier, not on your body.
Blank scar plates aren't any use to you yet. The Cerebral Scarring Station opens at the fourth Degree.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.scar_st: The Cerebral Scarring Station carves a route into a blank scar. You give it the template and its catalyst, and it does the cutting.
The station only makes the instruction. Getting it into your practice is the Vein-Mason's business: their rite, the Effigy and the Brazier.
The Cerebral Scarring Station opens at the fourth Degree. Come back when you're there.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.slime_b: Slime's sticky elasticity looks a lot like Ductilis, which matters to nobody unless a working recipe calls for it.
Resemblance alone won't get you anything out of a centrifuge, so don't feed it slime and hope.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.somatic: The Somatic Loom takes a blank Hematic Memory, the exact catalyst, stored enzyme units, and projected blood.

Once the blood's paid, the engram spreads across the floor with its fragments waiting at the points of a star. Use the Living Staff to thread each one home along the star's lines. Every step spins out a span of enzyme thread, so a tidy route costs you less.
You're not far enough into your initiation for the Somatic Loom. Come back at the third Degree.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.specime: That's a sealed living specimen. I can tell you what's in there. The jar hasn't made it harmless, though.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.spore_s: A concentrated fungal specimen. Keep it sealed tight, because dry doesn't mean dead.
Use it in fungal recipes and cultures. At Degree 4, Hyphal Substrate seated in a Cardinal Focus lets a Working floor forge a Fungal Implantation Pylon.
hemomancy.alchemist.item_inquiry.unknown: Nothing I work with. Ask whoever made it.
hemomancy.alchemist.living_bestiary.intr: The Red Taxonomy covers rooted things, and the Living Bestiary gets everything that tries to leave the jar.
Bring me Hemomancy fauna in specimen jars. I'll record the creature and give it back, or keep the specimen for dissection and compensate you for it.
Got an empty jar? Use it on a Chitinite and you'll see how capture works. Rooted specimens don't go in a jar, so bring those to me by hand.
hemomancy.alchemist.living_bestiary.morp: Wild Morphling Polyps haven't settled into a strain yet. Where one grows decides which partner organisms it's picked up, and the partner decides the strain.
Surrender a captured polyp and you get a matching wild-bound morphling. It's useful, but it stays capped until an Incubator stabilizes it.
hemomancy.alchemist.living_bestiary.reco: Keep the specimen in one piece. I don't need it, just the observations entered in your Bestiary.
hemomancy.alchemist.living_bestiary.surr: Surrender the jar and the study uses up the specimen. Are you sure you're done with it?
Which living layer are you surrendering? Whichever polyp you pick gets used up in the study.
hemomancy.alchemist.machines_overview: Learn them in order: the Centrifuge separates sampled blood, the Alembic distills reagents, and the Loom's where prepared memories get woven. Each machine assumes you survived the one before it.
hemomancy.alchemist.morphling_handling.i: Have the Alchemist inspect your captured Polyp or earlier Bestiary record. You keep the jar and the specimen.
hemomancy.alchemist.morphling_handling.l: Got an empty Specimen Jar? Capture a wild Morphling Polyp in it and come back with the filled jar in your main hand. If I've already recorded a Polyp for your Bestiary, that study counts.
hemomancy.alchemist.morphling_handling.r: You've brought a Polyp, or I've already got your Bestiary record. Either way I can mark the handling study without taking another specimen.
The Alchemist records your Morphling handling. You keep the specimen.
hemomancy.alchemist.morphling_handling.t: This is field handling, nothing more. Incubation comes later, and that's the Incubator's job.
hemomancy.alchemist.neophyte.blood_gourd: You'll want a blood gourd later, but the Vicar's first bloodcraft proof doesn't need one. Can you absorb and project blood yet? Learn that first, and we'll talk about a vessel once you can use it.
hemomancy.alchemist.neophyte.centrifuge_: The Vial Centrifuge comes after the Vicar grants you Degree 2. Until then, find out what Blood Absorption and Projection can make in your own hands.
hemomancy.alchemist.neophyte.line1: §7[The Alchemist looks at your hands before they look at your face]
hemomancy.alchemist.neophyte.line2: Neophyte, are you? Your bloodcraft proof and the second Degree are the Vicar's business, and I've got something smaller. Draw a few clean samples from ordinary animals and hang on to them. You'll want them for the Centrifuge later.
hemomancy.alchemist.pallid_vessel.offer: Initiate, you'll want a reserve that doesn't live in your own veins. So make the Pallid Vessel, the first blood gourd, and show me it works.
hemomancy.alchemist.pallid_vessel.progre: Your first vessel's on record. The red one comes at Degree 4, and it starts from that white gourd and an Amethyst Shard.
Your rite's on record, so the gourd exists. Now it needs blood in it. Set it in the Alembic's blood-output slot, let it draw, then take it back out.
Rite on record, gourd holding blood. That's a clean run from start to finish. Let me look at it, then you can have it back.
Nothing on your record yet. Did you perform the rite yourself? A gourd someone hands you won't count, so here's the procedure again.
hemomancy.alchemist.pallid_vessel.record: The Alchemist adds the Pallid Vessel to your ledger.
The Alchemist records the Pallid Vessel and sets aside two Dried Gourds and an Amethyst Shard for you.
Your ledger records blood in the White Blood Gourd.
Your ledger records the Rite of the Pallid Vessel.
hemomancy.alchemist.pallid_vessel.report: Show the Alchemist your filled White Blood Gourd. You keep the gourd and its blood.
hemomancy.alchemist.pallid_vessel.steps: Then put blood in the white gourd. The Ghastly Alembic's blood-output slot will do it, or a Gourdvine Tap. It holds 1,000 mL, and any amount proves the seal. Bring it back and I'll mark the run. This is bench work. Your third-Degree proof is the Woven Vessel, and it doesn't wait on this.
hemomancy.alchemist.phlegethontic_commis: Taking the Nether position that lines up with yours, there's a Basin about %s blocks %s. Look for banks of blackstone around dark ichor.
I can't line up a Nether bearing from the End. Ask me again from the Overworld or the Nether.
I can't find a Basin within about 8,000 Nether blocks of your aligned position. Ask again from another Nether reach.

There are basins of dark ichor in the Nether, banked with blackstone and growth that looks alive. The place reads as nearly organic to me, but that's my interpretation, and I wouldn't write it down as fact about the Nether.
The Alchemist records the Basin comparison and returns the sample and all five Scyphus.
Show the Alchemist the Basin blood sample and five Scyphus. Nothing is used up.
You've got blood from a Basin creature? Good. Bring enough Scyphus to show me and I'll compare the sample against the local growth.

I need blood from an Excoriated or Phlegethontic Bombardier, plus five Escharian Scyphus you've gathered yourself. Sample, then sneak-use the Living Syringe to eject its rack. Use the rack on an idle Vial Centrifuge and remove the vial without spinning it. Hold that vial in your main hand when you show me, and I'll inspect it and give everything back. It's field work, and it isn't my permission to enter the Nether.
hemomancy.alchemist.preparations.alembic: Distill Sanguine Formation in the base Alembic with the aligned enzyme as catalyst. The blood comes out of the stored tank, and the tincture needs somewhere to go, so put an empty clay flask or jug in the lower-right container input. You'll qualify for the Condenser at the fourth Degree and the Athanor at the sixth, and they both upgrade the same Alembic.
hemomancy.alchemist.preparations.briefed: I gave you Sanguine Formation, Fervent Enzyme and a Bloody Flask for Body Answers. If you've already distilled the tincture, drink it and you're done, with no need to brew it again.
hemomancy.alchemist.preparations.capacit: A tincture teaches your body a Thelemic memory. It goes in the Reliquary next to what the Mnemonist calls your Noetic memories, and they share one active capacity. If you want to weave a Noetic memory on purpose, that's the Loom's job.
hemomancy.alchemist.preparations.complet: You've drunk the first tincture, so Body Answers is done. The other seven Thelemic preparations use the same base formula, each with its own aligned enzyme.
hemomancy.alchemist.preparations.title: What should I make in the Alembic now?
hemomancy.alchemist.preparations.unbrief: You might've distilled a tincture already during your second-Degree work. Body Answers comes after First Separation, and its first preparation is Sanguine Fists, a tincture you drink. The Loom has nothing to do with it.
hemomancy.alchemist.purifying.explain: §7[The Alchemist doesn't look up]§r There's nothing to explain. Every hour you spend on that path is an hour you aren't learning these machines, and I've got a rack to finish.
hemomancy.alchemist.purifying.line1: §7[The Alchemist glances up from their work, looks you over for a moment, and turns back to their instruments, face blank]
hemomancy.alchemist.purifying.line2: I don't have time to teach someone who won't use it. You're purging the very thing these machines run on. Which is it going to be? Come back when you've decided.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.bleedin: Bleeding Heart, a flower grown into the shape of the body's vessels. Whatever infected it knew what a vein looks like.
See the hanging wound-shape? That's vascular mimicry. The plant's copied the outline of an injury with no idea what grief is.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.devils_: Devil's Tooth is a defensive fruiting expression. Its exudate looks like blood, and under stress it'll start behaving like blood too.
Caustic secretion and a tooth-shaped point. I don't need a Mnemonist to tell me that means hands off.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.infecte: Infected Fungus is the baseline sample, ordinary fungal tissue that's been taught to carry hemomantic instruction.
It's common, and that's what makes it useful, since it shows you what the blood-fungus does when it's got nothing to prove.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.intro.l: You're a Votary now, so I'm putting you on field samples. Blood-touched fungi, or flora that's nearly fungal. Bring me what you find.
Any order is fine: Infected Fungus, Stinkhorn, Sarcodes, Bleeding Heart, Rafflesia, Devil's Tooth, and Puffball as a control. I'll catalog each one as it comes in.
Whatever's left over sorts into three lanes. Bleeding Heart and Sarcodes make Bleeding Bulbs. Infected Fungus, Stinkhorn and Devil's Tooth make Foul Paste, and Puffball and Rafflesia make Spore Sacs.
A sampled Fungling also separates into Infected Fungus. Mix Foul Paste into a log for Infested Wood, then keep the space above it empty and dark so the culture can grow.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.puffbal: Puffball is the control. It's less dramatic and less devotional, which is why it's useful.
An assay needs contrast. If every specimen on the bench is screaming, how would you know what a whisper sounds like?
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.raffles: Rafflesia is theft on an architectural scale, a bloom living off a body it never meant to repay.
Look at the size of it. Give a small parasite enough appetite and enough patience and it'll turn into a structure.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.sarcode: Sarcodes feeds through networks it didn't build. Elegant and unpleasant, and frankly very Harbinger.
It reads another plant's plumbing well enough to make it pay.
hemomancy.alchemist.red_taxonomy.stinkho: Stinkhorn spreads by smell. Anything that comes sniffing round it leaves carrying the blood-fungus.
It doesn't have to catch anything. A carrier that'll walk toward the wrong scent is enough, and there's never a shortage of those.
That's one of the blood-fed fungi I asked for. Hand it over and I'll add the result to your taxonomy.
hemomancy.alchemist.sanctified.curved_ho: At Degree 6, offer the black gourd with dragon's breath on a Grand Working floor, with the required Hematic Iron Pillars in place, then fill its four anchors, wake the required Bastion support sigil and project into the daemon. The horn holds 1,500 mL and lets it go in a hurry. Your capacity stops growing there. If the rite succeeds, it costs you the earlier vessel and the pillars.
hemomancy.alchemist.sanctified.final_mac: By now the machines are one process. The Alembic distills with what the Centrifuge separates, the Centrifuge's enzymes stock the Loom, and the Loom writes the result into memory. Run every station and you can make anything I can.
hemomancy.alchemist.sanctified.line1: Sanctified now, and at the threshold of the Hematic Order. The machines have given you everything they can for now. What's left is the final synthesis, and I've only ever read the notes on it.
hemomancy.alchemist.thelemic_memory_cata: There are seven preparations left. Each one takes Sanguine Formation, blood stored in the Alembic, and an empty clay flask or jug in its container input. Match the catalyst to the tendency you want your body to remember.
Ferric is for labor, Neurotic for motion, Umbral for silence, Incandescent for sight, Vivacious for the heart, Frigid for endurance and Ruinous for carrion.
A compatible Morphling makes the answer cheaper and easier on you, and some strains add a reflex of their own. None of this locks in your final path.
hemomancy.alchemist.uninitiated.line1: §7[A figure in stained work robes glances up from a crowded rig of vessels and tubing, keeping one hand on a valve]
hemomancy.alchemist.uninitiated.line2: Mind the tubing. I'm the Harbinger Alchemist. I keep this Outpost's machines running, which mostly means talking blood into doing something useful. You aren't initiated, so none of this would work for you yet.
hemomancy.alchemist.uninitiated.machines: These machines respond to blood that's been refined through the Covenant's rites. Earn your first Degree and I'll teach you what each one does.
hemomancy.alchemist.votary.alembic_lore: You can study the Ghastly Alembic now. It distills plants, fungi and creature matter into defined reagents, and whether a batch answers cleanly depends on the fire, the state of the vessel and the recipe.
hemomancy.alchemist.votary.centrifuge_lo: The Vial Centrifuge does the first separation: sampled vials go in balanced and come out as one of eight enzyme expressions. At your Degree you've also got the Ghastly Alembic, which opens up the wider work of reagent distillation.
hemomancy.alchemist.votary.first_distill: Make a Ghastly Alembic, run one ordinary distillation through it and take the result. First Separation proves you can recover an enzyme, and the Alembic proves you can use blood as a reagent. Once you've done both, ask me for Concentrated Blood.
hemomancy.alchemist.votary.gourd_upgrade: Your gourd should keep pace with you. Upgrade it whenever your rites allow, and keep going after the first one, because a stronger vessel means deeper reserves and steadier casting.
hemomancy.alchemist.votary.line1: A Votary. Your blood's starting to lean toward a tendency, and the Vial Centrifuge is where you'll see which way.
hemomancy.altar.already_blessed: The altar has already blessed you. Our Lady's tears flow only once.
hemomancy.altar.blessed: §bThe Tears of Silthmere wash over the altar, and silver light floods your veins as Our Lady's blessing purifies you.
hemomancy.altar.brew_exhausted: §7The altar has drawn all it can from your Lethean Brew offerings.
hemomancy.altar.brew_offered: §7The altar's flame consumes the Lethean Brew. Memories fade and your purity grows.
hemomancy.altar.chalice_already_offered: §7Your silver chalice offering has already been accepted.
hemomancy.altar.chalice_offered: §bThe silver chalice rings with a pure tone, and your clarity deepens.
hemomancy.altar.clarity_not_unlocked: The chalice resonates, but you haven't unlocked clarity yet.
hemomancy.altar.icon_already_offered: The altar has already accepted a Pallid Icon from you. Its power flows only once.
hemomancy.altar.icon_offered: §bThe Pallid Icon blazes with silver fire on the altar, and clarity surges through you.
hemomancy.altar.lore: §7A cool mist rises from the stone. You sense Our Lady of Still Waters close by.
hemomancy.altar.not_on_path: The altar stays silent. Only those on the Unstained path can hear it.
hemomancy.altar.wreath_already_offered: §7Your Lethean Poppy Wreath offering has already been accepted.
hemomancy.altar.wreath_offered: §7The Lethean poppies wilt on the altar as the stone draws in their essence. Your purity rises.
hemomancy.anchorite.carve_reminder.line1: Still uncut. Set the pattern in the Cerebral Scarring Station and follow its grid cell by cell.
hemomancy.anchorite.carve_reminder.line2: Load Pattern shows a purple stencil. Trace those cells in red and press Carve. A rejected carving keeps your work, so correct it and carve again. Put the carved Scar in an empty, lit Iron Brazier with ordinary use. A cold Brazier lights with Blood Projection for 50 mL. Then hold Blood Absorption on the Scar. Learning it costs you 100 mL. The old template alone will teach you nothing.
hemomancy.anchorite.completed.line1: There. The wound has become architecture.
hemomancy.anchorite.completed.line2: You can work other patterns now. Before each cut, find out what it opens in your body and what it closes.
Take the next pattern when you are ready to choose your own cuts.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.activation: Distill a Thelemic dose and drink it. Equip its memory, select it, and press your manipulation-use key to turn it on. Its ordinary bodily action spends blood and reserve as it works. Crouch and press that key, and the next response is armed for overexertion. That costs twice the blood and two-and-a-half times the strain.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.cause_strain: Use a Thelemic Memory until one section turns Varicose. It has to be your body's own instruction. A sword cut or projected will does not count.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.complete: You took the strain, let me read it, treated it and then fortified, all in the right order. Take the deeper pattern.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.diagnosis.prompt: Hold still. I will find the worst of the damage before you treat anything, and then you will know which medicine it needs.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.fortify: The medicine puts back what you spent, and that is all it does. Hematic Fortification cuts your vascular strain by 15% for good. Work that rite of the fourth Degree, then come back. The diagnosis and treatment you already did still count.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.recover: If one course is failing, the Alchemist's Salve is enough. If two are, use the Poultice, which spreads across both. Clotting, or Varicosity spread wide through you, needs Vascular Mending.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.return_diagnosis: The current is catching somewhere in you. Let me find where, and you treat that. Most people reach for whatever worked last time.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.reward.prompt: This one cuts deeper than the last. I would not give it to someone who had skipped a step.
hemomancy.anchorite.d5.stop: Keep Vascular Status open on the body section it names. The moment it first turns Varicose, below 50 health, stop. Press the use key again without crouching to switch the memory off. Bring Salve before you train. Come back to me for diagnosis before you treat anything, because rest alone can change the medicine you need. Nothing you earn in this lesson is taken back.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.change_loadout: Now change it. Prepare a different arrangement at the Mason's Effigy and burn it, so your active scar set is not the one you started with.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.complete: The current changed because you changed its banks. The final pattern is ready.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.first_route: Keep a cerebral scar active that matches a Noetic Memory's primary tendency, and cast that memory. It has to come out of you. Mechanical projections do not count.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.referral: A scar can route an instruction through you. What the instruction says is a Mnemonist's craft. Take my question to one of them.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.referral.prompt: Go and ask the Mnemonist, and hear their counsel out. Then come back here and prove the route to me.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.reward.prompt: This is the last pattern I will give you, and the hardest to carve. Take it when you want it.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.second_route: Cast another matching Noetic Memory through the new arrangement. If it carries that, the change held.
hemomancy.anchorite.d6.seek_counsel: You have not been to the Mnemonist yet. Go to them first. Once they have told you what the memory means, I can work out how your body carries it.
hemomancy.anchorite.effigy_instruction.l: Good. It took. Now the Mason's Effigy, which lays out scars your blood already remembers. Whoever charges a motif must know all its scars and have room for them.

Make Runic Motif Paper from Paper, Charcoal and a Sanguine Formation. At the Mason's Effigy, choose your known scar and press Prepare, then lay the paper on and project 500 mL for each scar. Selection stays fixed while it charges. You may stop and resume. If you break the Effigy, it returns its paper, not spent blood. Take the prepared Pattern to the Brazier after. Nothing is set in you until it burns there.
hemomancy.anchorite.first_lesson.given.l: The pattern marks the cut. Once the scar is cut, the blood uses it.

Carve the Scar item first and burn it, in that order. The Mason's Effigy can prepare a living motif only after that. For this first scar you may use a nearby Scarring Station, while I watch you. Every pattern after it needs a station you built with your own hand.
hemomancy.anchorite.first_lesson.line1: They call me the Vein-Mason. I show a body where it is going to break, and then I mend it around the break so it can carry more.
hemomancy.anchorite.first_lesson.line2: I start everyone on their strongest tendency. Here is an old Scar Pattern cut for yours. Carve it at the Cerebral Scarring Station.
hemomancy.anchorite.first_lesson.line3: A blank plate, the catalyst, a knapper and the pattern. When it is carved, the scar goes in an empty, lit Iron Brazier. That is where you find out whether it becomes memory.
hemomancy.anchorite.first_lesson.prompt: Take the pattern, then, and carve it at the Scarring Station the way I told you. Do not rush the grid.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.blank_memory: The Mnemonist will put something in that. My concern is the road it takes through your body afterwards.
If what they write and what I cut do not match, you are the one who tears.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.blank_scar.l: A Blank Scar. Prepared tissue, waiting for somebody to cut an authored pattern into it.
The Artificer reinforces what faces the world. I reinforce what must carry the current within.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.brazier.line: The Iron Brazier does two jobs. It teaches you a carved scar, or it commits a pattern from the Effigy.

Put one offering in with ordinary use, then light the Brazier with Blood Projection for 50 mL. Hold Blood Absorption on the lit offering until it dissolves. Learning a carved Scar costs 100 mL, and committing a prepared Pattern costs 50 mL. Sneak if you want to retrieve the offering unburned.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.conductive_m: Conductive Mark. A Noetic Memory, so it is projected, and its primary tendency leads it.
Keep an active cerebral scar that matches it, and the route it takes through your vessels carries less strain.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.effigy.line1: The Effigy works with scars you have already burned into memory. It lays them out as a set.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.effigy.line2: The set does nothing in you until you burn the prepared motif at an Iron Brazier, and then it is active.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.gauge.line1: Read the number beside the flow state. The gauge tells you what is wrong, and fixing it is still up to you.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.gauge.line2: Hover over a section and it shows which Noetic and Thelemic routes are loading it.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.pattern.line: A Scar Pattern is the drawing you carve from. Take it to the station and cut it. Once the scars are learned, lay them out at the Effigy.
Tier-three patterns still need Deep Inscription before you can cut them.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.poultice.lin: The Poultice spreads its repair over your two weakest sections at once.
If you see clotting, put the Salve and Poultice away and do Vascular Mending properly.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.salve.line1: The Alchemist's Salve closes one local failure. Field medicine. It will not make you stronger.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.salve.line2: Use it when one section falls below Stable.
hemomancy.anchorite.inquiry.tier_one.lin: One of the first patterns. While it is active it deepens one tendency, and a Noetic Memory of the same tendency can route through it.
A memory routed through it costs you five percent less strain. Two matching scars share the one route rather than adding up, and only the strongest route counts.
hemomancy.anchorite.item_hint: Put it on the table, and I will tell you what it asks of your body.
hemomancy.anchorite.loadout_reminder.lin: The Effigy has done its part, and the motif is written. Burn it at the Brazier and you will learn whether that arrangement can live in you.

Same as before. Put the prepared Scar Pattern in an empty, lit Iron Brazier with ordinary use, and light a cold one with Blood Projection for 50 mL. Hold Blood Absorption on it. The commit costs another 50 mL and changes your active cerebral loadout. You know the scar already, so nothing is learned this time.
hemomancy.anchorite.locked.line1: Not yet. Carve into you now and it would slump like wet clay.
hemomancy.anchorite.locked.line2: Come back at the fourth Degree, with your blood active. A scar is a sympathetic wound, and your mind has to come through it in one piece.
hemomancy.anchorite.opinion.alchemist.li: The Alchemist mends damaged tissue, with Salve and Poultice. When you are hurt, go to them first.
I work after them, on what the mended body can bear next time. You need both of us, usually in that order.
hemomancy.anchorite.opinion.artificer.li: The Artificer works on the outside of you: the plate, the weapon, the frame and the graft.
I work on the inside, where nobody sees the joins. If an instruction tears something on its way through you, it was my work that failed.
hemomancy.anchorite.refusal.line1: Still-water has touched you. A scar cut into that body would fight itself, and cruelly.
hemomancy.anchorite.refusal.line2: Scar-work is for those who still bargain with blood-memory, and you have stopped. I will not cut you.
hemomancy.anchorite.replace_pattern.prom: Lost it already? I can replace the last pattern I gave you. Do not ask me for spares.
hemomancy.anchorite.reward.claimed.line1: Carve it when your body can afford one more instruction.
hemomancy.anchorite.reward.claimed.line2: The Motif Paper lets you change your scar loadout later. Look at what sits next to what before you burn it.
hemomancy.anchorite.reward.line1: That will hold. You have been round the whole cycle once now.
hemomancy.anchorite.reward.line2: Your strongest tendency picked the first pattern for you. This second old pattern is for the tendency under it. Learn it, and then start choosing for yourself.
hemomancy.annetta.ally.0: Stay close. I can still mend you.
hemomancy.annetta.ally.1: It knows my name. Don't let it say it.
hemomancy.annetta.ally.3: I carried that? All this time?
hemomancy.annetta.break.last_words: If it wants me so badly, then-
hemomancy.annetta.cowering.harbinger_hin: Keep those things away from me. I know what they do. I'd know that smell anywhere.
[Her eyes stay on your hands. She's looking for glass, and for teeth that move.]
hemomancy.annetta.cowering.neutral.line1: [Annetta is pressed into the corner, knuckles white on the hilt of a small dagger. Her red hair hangs down over her face.]
hemomancy.annetta.cowering.neutral.line2: No. No more tests, and no more questions. Please. Leave me here, where the walls are still.
hemomancy.annetta.cowering.unstained_hin: If you came from the still waters, you know why I can't pray cleanly anymore.
I'll drink anything if it makes the noise stop. I'm so tired of being proof.
hemomancy.annetta.cured_support.line1: [Her hair has gone white, but her hands no longer shake. She keeps herself between you and the thing she used to carry.]
hemomancy.annetta.cured_support.line2: Stay close. I can slow it down and keep you breathing. You'll have to finish what the mercy started.
hemomancy.annetta.draught.line1: [You hold out the Draught of Still Mercy. She stares at its still surface.]
hemomancy.annetta.draught.line2: Is that from the waters? It smells like the river at dawn.
hemomancy.annetta.draught.truth.line1: There's something inside you, Annetta. You've been carrying it a long time.
hemomancy.annetta.draught.truth.line2: [Her hands go to her neck, then fall.]
hemomancy.annetta.draught.truth.line3: Then take it. Take it, even if it pulls me apart.
hemomancy.annetta.event.bitten: The jar breaks open and a Tooth Peck bites into her. Annetta screams as something she never knew she carried tears awake.
hemomancy.annetta.event.burst: She drives the dagger into the swollen thing at her neck. It bursts, and takes everything above her shoulders with it.
hemomancy.annetta.event.cured: The draught takes hold. The red drains out of her hair while the infection she carried tears itself loose.
hemomancy.annetta.event.falter: Annetta staggers. Her shield slips from her arm.
hemomancy.annetta.event.mutation: What is left of Annetta rises out of the blood, and it is not her.
hemomancy.annetta.event.no_room: There isn't enough room here for what would tear out of her, so you keep the draught in your hand.
hemomancy.annetta.event.reanimating: The blood around her body is moving.
hemomancy.annetta.event.resolved: The infection comes apart, and Annetta is still standing when it's gone.
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.0: Get it off, get it OFF me!
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.1: Lady, still my hands. Still my hands.
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.2: What did you put in me?
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.3: I was clean. I was clean every morning.
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.4: Stop looking at me like that!
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.5: It's drinking. I can feel it drinking.
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.6: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, stay back!
hemomancy.annetta.frantic.7: The water was supposed to keep me.
hemomancy.annetta.jar.line1: [Her eyes go to the jar before they go to you.]
hemomancy.annetta.jar.line2: Those things. They follow me, they always follow me.
hemomancy.annetta.jar.line3: Please. Whatever they want in me, I don't have it.
hemomancy.annetta.purge.pulling: Something is pulling. It's pulling out of me!
hemomancy.annetta.resolved.how_long.line: Since the church was whole, I think. Since before I took the white.
The Tooth Pecks knew all along. I thought they were a test.
[She touches her white hair.] I was proof, all right. Just not of what I believed.
hemomancy.annetta.resolved.line1: [Annetta looks at the broken nave without flinching.]
hemomancy.annetta.resolved.line2: I remember being afraid in here, and being wrong. For now that'll have to be enough.
hemomancy.annetta.resolved.what_now.line: Mend what I can. Sit with the ones who come here sick and ask me to make them clean.
And when I'm ready, I'll go back to the water and tell them what it looks like from inside.
hemomancy.antecedent.cylinder.descriptio: An old ambergris cylinder cut with unfamiliar grooves. Play it in a Clairaudiograph, and bring an analyzed dark sample.
hemomancy.antecedent.cylinder.lower_dist: Weathered Ambergris Cylinder: Lower District Survey
hemomancy.antecedent.cylinder.playback_h: Ancient recording. Playback preserves the cylinder and any specimen.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.clue.1: The account points to a quiet place below the city, past the end of a wool-lined passage, where the Last Listeners kept watch.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.clue.2: Follow the Ancient City roads and look for a small, enclosed entrance, which could be beside any district. Go through the passage, and when the wool stops, keep going.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.clue.3: Leave the damaged structures alone while you're there, since a missing piece may be the reason the growth can't answer itself.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.clue.4: I don't know if their work held because they did it well or because nobody has tried to undo it. Please don't test that by putting anything back together.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.clue.title: Where did the Last Listeners keep vigil?
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.comparison: I see why you ask, but I can't tell you they came from the same Entity when, so far, the similarities are only on the surface.
The sculk sample has no blood and answers none of the eight tendencies. The Alchemist can't draw an enzyme from it. Erythromycelium is made of something else entirely.
Their behavior gives us a better question. How does each one spread, and what does it need to stay alive?
Sculk stays in one area and feeds on the dead, while Erythromycelium moves through living hosts, and we'd need much stronger evidence than that to claim they share an origin.
Could the Antecedent be the same Entity?
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.conclusion: I was wrong about the sample. Sound makes it move, but it also turned toward the machine when the recording fell silent.
The sound trace stayed flat the whole time. Something was still present in the grooves, and the sample seemed to sense it.
I can't tell you what that signal is. Our machine may be missing part of the sound, or the old recording may carry something else entirely.
The speaker also said they stopped the growth from answering itself without killing it. The Vicar may know what they meant. Take him the cylinder and the vial.
What did the controlled replay establish?
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.housing.1: The archive shows how they built a small listening device, and if you bring me four iron nuggets and one Echo Shard, I'll make its housing.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.housing.2: Hold the housing in one hand and an analyzed Ahaematic vial in the other, then use the housing to load it. Keep it beside the Clairaudiograph through the full silent section, and when it wakes, you can fit it to your Charm at a Scarlet Vanity or take it off there later.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.initial_al: Let me see that vial. My microscope can't find a blood cell in it, but the material inside keeps moving together.
Tap the glass for me. See how it pulls back? I tested all eight tendencies, and none of them fit. I don't know what we're looking at.
The Vicar once warned me away from a similar account in the old histories. Take the sample to him and see if he remembers it.
Keep the vial. Try to learn what makes the material move, and search an Ancient City for records left by people who lived near it.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.initial_vi: The Alchemist sent you because the sample doesn't behave like blood, and they're right to ask, though I can't name it from a vial alone.
There's a passage I know that might describe something like it, but it's old and vague, and I don't want to build a history around one sample.
Go to an Ancient City and look for something its people recorded for themselves, because an instruction or a field report would tell us more than any later account could.
Bring back whatever you find, along with the vial, so I can compare the words with what the sample does.
The Alchemist sent me with this dark sample.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.recognitio: Did you hear it? The speaker says they stopped the growth from answering itself, yet it stayed alive, and I've seen that same account in our oldest histories.
Those histories describe a wound that never healed and living material that remained beneath it. They say the break held, but they never explain what was broken.
There's no author, no date and no named rite. By the Second Age people read it as a lesson in restraint, and so did I, but this recording makes that reading harder to accept.
If the speaker meant the sculk, they may have cut off a way for its parts to answer each other. The growth could survive even after that connection was gone.
That's still a guess. We've seen it react to a recording, and we haven't proved that it speaks, remembers or understands us.
Later writers called these fragments the Antecedent because they seem to describe something older than blood. We don't know what the people in that city called it.

Find the place where they watched the damaged growth, because their own records may tell us what they tried to separate and why they left the sculk alive. Ask me about the Last Listeners when you're ready.
What did the old recording mean?
This cylinder is ambergris, but those grooves came from a different machine, so the people who made it knew how to store a recording too.
You said part of it went silent? I can see another trace there on the spectrograph, even though our machine plays no sound from that section.
Bring your analyzed dark sample back. Put it in the Clairaudiograph or hold it beside the machine, then play the cylinder again.
After that, set the machine within eight blocks of me so I can watch a full replay. If the sample only reacts to sound, it should sit still through the silent part.
I found an old recording beneath an Ancient City.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.replay.1: The sample climbed the glass toward the machine? When, during the Shrieker or after it? During the silence, you say. All right, let me see it.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.replay.2: I want to watch that happen myself. Set up the cylinder again.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.replay.3: Put the analyzed vial beside the machine and play the whole silent section while I'm within eight blocks. Watch the sound trace and the other one.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.replay.4: If the vial moves while the sound trace stays flat, we'll know ordinary sound isn't causing it.
hemomancy.antecedent.dialogue.replay.tit: The sample reacted during the silence.
hemomancy.antecedent.epilogue:
You found us under the stone.

We remember listening here, waiting for the dead to come. We waited a long time.

We don't wait for them now.
hemomancy.antecedent.housing.cost: Reconstruction needs four iron nuggets and one Echo Shard.
